# Roadmap

pitfight (formerly the working name bot-arena; CLI command `pit`): a Core War-style programming game. Players write small bots for a tiny virtual machine; the bots share a circular memory arena and try to make each other crash. v1 is the ISA spec, assembler, deterministic VM and arena, tournament runner, replay format, and terminal and web viewers, in Go (standard library only) with a plain JavaScript + canvas web viewer. Source: PROJECT.md and the owner decisions of 2026-10-15 (C26-C37).

## Goals

Goal records C01-C07 come from PROJECT.md Goals. The open decisions, first filed as assumptions C20-C25, were settled by the owner on 2026-10-15 in S01 as decisions C26-C33 (name, ISA, core language, replay format, default match parameters, visualizer priority, license, CI deferred), with constraints C34-C37 (in-repo Go caches and local checks, implementer-recorded interface details, determinism rules, Go fuzzing).

### C01 Small, well-specified instruction set with a written spec

A small, well-specified instruction set with a written spec. Compatibility with the Redcode standard vs a new ISA is an open decision. (PROJECT.md Goals 1)

### C02 Assembler with labels, expressions and line-numbered errors

An assembler with labels, expressions, and clear error messages with line numbers. (PROJECT.md Goals 2)

### C03 Deterministic VM

The same bots, seed and config always give the same result, which makes replays and tests possible. (PROJECT.md Goals 3)

### C04 Arena with seeded placement, round-robin scheduling, cycle limit and tie rule

An arena with N bots, random non-overlapping start positions from a seed, round-robin process scheduling, a cycle limit and a defined tie rule. (PROJECT.md Goals 4)

### C05 Reproducible tournament runner with scoreboard

Round-robin over many seeds, a scoreboard, reproducible results. (PROJECT.md Goals 5)

### C06 Terminal and web visualizer of recorded replays

A terminal view and a web view of memory ownership and execution pointers, with step, play, pause and seek on recorded replays. (PROJECT.md Goals 6)

### C07 Compact versioned replay format

Compact, versioned, and able to drive the visualizer without re-simulating. (PROJECT.md Goals 7)

## Constraints

### C12 VM core is pure

The VM core has no I/O, no clocks, and uses seeded RNG only for placement. Everything else wraps it. (PROJECT.md Architecture sketch)

### C13 Every dependency needs owner approval

Standard library first. Every third-party Go module, toolchain (including tsc for TypeScript), wasm toolchain or JS package needs owner approval with a stated reason and a FLOSS license. The Go toolchain itself (go1.27.2) and its stock GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm target are approved by C28. (PROJECT.md Dependency / licensing notes, Risks: Toolchain; updated for C28)

### C14 Do not bundle existing warriors until licensing is checked

ICWS standards and existing warriors are public material, but their licensing has to be checked before bundling any existing warriors. Not verified yet. (PROJECT.md Dependency / licensing notes)

### C34 Go caches stay in the repo; local checks

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (carried over from the owner's sibling project). `scripts/env.sh` exports GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE, GOPATH, GOTMPDIR and TMPDIR under a gitignored `.cache/` in the repo, plus GOTOOLCHAIN=local and GOPROXY=off. Every Go command runs with it sourced (`. scripts/env.sh && go ...`). The project checks are `go test ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l cmd internal` (must print nothing).

### C35 Implementer decides unfixed interface details and records them

Owner decision 2026-10-15 (standing rule). Interface details not fixed by PROJECT.md or a catalog decision (for example package APIs, CLI flags and output formats, syntax details) are decided by the slice implementer and recorded in the catalog as a decision with a one-line reason. The reviewer checks each one.

### C36 Determinism: no map iteration in core; in-repo seeded PRNG

Owner decision 2026-10-15. No map iteration in the VM or arena core (Go map order is randomized). Randomness comes only from an in-repo seeded PRNG with a fixed, documented algorithm, not math/rand or math/rand/v2, so results and replays survive Go upgrades. Extends C12 and C03.

### C37 Use Go built-in fuzzing where natural

Owner decision 2026-10-15. Go's built-in fuzzing (`go test -fuzz`) needs no dependency. Use it for the assembler and VM where a slice benefits. Fuzz targets keep a seed corpus so plain `go test ./...` runs them as regular tests.

### C40 pit usage handling: stderr+exit 2 for no args or unknown subcommand, help on stdout

Implementer decision under C35 (S02). `pit` with no arguments prints usage to stderr and exits 2; `pit help` prints usage to stdout and exits 0; an unknown subcommand prints `pit: unknown subcommand "X"`, a blank line and the usage to stderr, exit 2. The usage lists asm, run, tourney, view and help as planned, and states exit codes 0 success, 2 usage error (1 is reserved for a failed operation in later slices). Planned subcommands that are not built yet also report unknown. Reason: it matches the slice text and the shell convention that usage errors are 2 and requested help is 0; the planned-not-built case disappears as each subcommand lands.

### C41 scripts/env.sh needs bash or zsh and refuses to run outside a repo root

Implementer decision under C35 (S02), accepted by the owner 2026-10-15, overriding the slice's 'POSIX sh, no bashisms' text. A sourced POSIX script cannot learn its own path, so env.sh reads BASH_SOURCE or zsh's %x, derives the repo root from it, clears CDPATH for the cd, and exports nothing and creates nothing unless that root holds go.mod and scripts/env.sh (otherwise it prints an error and returns 1; dash fails the same way). It is sourced by absolute path from anywhere. Reason: the cache directories must follow the checkout (each worktree has its own .cache/) and a wrong or copied env.sh must never write Go caches elsewhere. env.sh does not set GOFLAGS=-modcacherw (the module has no dependencies); a slice that adds an approved dependency should revisit that.

### C43 ISA opcode set: 15 opcodes, codes in table order, no MOD or CMP

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). Opcodes in code order: DAT MOV ADD SUB MUL DIV JMP JMZ JMN DJN SPL SEQ SNE SLT NOP (codes 0..14). No MOD, LDP, STP or CMP alias. All 7 modifiers and 8 modes are valid with every opcode. Reason: the smallest Redcode-like set that still expresses imp, bomber, replicator and scanner, which keeps the spec to a few pages (C27, PROJECT.md); the code order is the order of the Go constants in internal/isa. Defined in docs/spec/isa.md section 3.

### C44 ISA modifiers and addressing-mode tokens: A B AB BA F X I; # $ * @ { < } >

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). Modifier mnemonics A B AB BA F X I (codes 0..6) and mode tokens # $ * @ { < } > (codes 0..7), with Redcode field pairing and mode meanings; I acts as F except for MOV, SEQ and SNE, where it covers the whole cell. DAT, JMP, SPL and NOP ignore the modifier. Reason: the owner chose an ISA strongly inspired by Redcode semantics (C27); familiar tokens let later Redcode compatibility reuse them and need no new vocabulary. docs/spec/isa.md section 3.

### C45 ISA numbers: CORESIZE 1..2^20, stored values int32 in [0,CORESIZE), arithmetic in int64

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). 1 <= CORESIZE <= 1048576; Norm(x) = ((x mod N) + N) mod N in int64; stored operand values are int32 in [0,N); written values are any integer, stored as Norm. Reason: int64 intermediates make ADD, SUB and MUL (up to 2^40) overflow-free for every allowed size, and the range includes the sizes 1, 8 and 8000 that the S05 tests name. docs/spec/isa.md section 1.

### C46 ISA empty cell is DAT.F $0, $0 with writer 0; bot ids start at 1

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). A fresh core cell is DAT.F $0, $0, writer 0 (no bot); bot ids are 1 and up; the writer is metadata that no instruction reads and SEQ.I/SNE.I ignore. Every cell write, including pre-decrement, post-increment and DJN decrement writes, sets the writer to the executing bot. Reason: matches the Redcode empty cell and makes unwritten core visible to the visualizer as owner 0 without a special value. docs/spec/isa.md section 2 and 4.

### C47 ISA step semantics: A then B evaluation with snapshots, post-increments after execute

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). A step fetches a copy IR, evaluates A (with pre-decrement writes) then B, taking a snapshot of each target at evaluation time; an immediate operand targets the executing cell; both operands are always evaluated; the opcode writes at most one cell; post-increments of A then B apply after execution, even if the process dies; then the process effect is appended. Reason: one fixed order makes events and worked cases unambiguous for the VM, replay and visualizer. Post-increment timing may differ from Redcode and is flagged in the spec. docs/spec/isa.md section 4.

### C48 ISA faults: only DAT and division by zero kill; DIV writes nothing if any divisor is 0

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). A process dies only by executing DAT or by DIV with a zero divisor in any of its pairs; in that case DIV writes nothing for any pair. Every cell content is legal, so there is no illegal-instruction fault. Reason: a single all-or-nothing rule is simpler to specify and test than Redcode's per-pair partial write. docs/spec/isa.md section 5.

### C49 ISA SPL at the process limit acts as a continue-only NOP

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). SPL appends PC+1 then the A target; if the bot already has MAXPROCESSES live processes (the executing one counts), only PC+1 is appended and nothing is signalled. The value and range of MAXPROCESSES are left to the match spec (S04). Reason: a failed spawn must not kill or error the bot, and the executing process counts so the cap is exact. docs/spec/isa.md section 5.

### C50 ISA spec table format and worked-case format (parsed by S06)

Implementer decision under C35 (S03). Three tables, each with header first column Mnemonic, the exact assembler token in backticks, rows in code order from 0 (opcodes, modifiers, addressing modes); no other table starts with Mnemonic. Worked cases are tables headed Case | Setup | Before | After | Queue; the Case id is OPCODE.MODIFIER[/suffix] or a mode mnemonic[/suffix]; Setup is N=<core size>[, MAXPROCESSES=<n>]; Before lists address: cell separated by semicolons with unlisted cells empty; After lists each write in order; Queue lists the addresses appended, [] for a dead bot. Reason: S06 parses these tables, so a fixed machine-readable layout lets it check that every entry has a test. Cases were checked against a scratch reference stepper outside the repo. docs/spec/isa.md sections 3 and 6.

### C51 Match defaults confirmed: core 8000, cycle limit 80000, max processes 8000

Implementer decision under C35 (S04). Verifies C30 on 2026-10-15: all three values are stated as defaults in the ICWS'94 draft predefined variables (https://corewar.info/lexicon/94draft.htm: CORESIZE 8000, MAXCYCLES 80000, MAXPROCESSES 8000) and on the 94 Standard Hill page (http://www.corewar.info/hills/94.htm: core size 8000, max cycles 80000, max processes 8000); the pMARS manual (https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/noble/man6/pmars.6.html) confirms 8000 for -s and -p and gives no -c default. Ranges: CORESIZE 1..2^20, CYCLELIMIT 1..2^31-1, MAXPROCESSES 1..2^20, MINSEPARATION 0..2^20, SEED any uint64 (default 0). Reason: two independent public sources agree on each value, so C30 no longer needs its unverified flag. docs/spec/match.md sections 1 and 2.

### C52 Match PRNG: SplitMix64, seed uint64, rejection-sampled Draw(n)

Implementer decision under C35 and C36 (S04). Generator is fixed-increment SplitMix64 (state += 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15; two xor-shift-multiply rounds with 0xBF58476D1CE4E5B9 and 0x94D049BB133111EB; final xor-shift 31), seed any uint64 including 0, all arithmetic modulo 2^64. Draw(n) for uint64 n>=1 rejects outputs below (2^64-n) mod n, so there is no modulo bias, and always consumes at least one output. Reason: a few lines of integer-only code with one 64-bit state and a published public-domain reference (https://prng.di.unimi.it/splitmix64.c), and rejection sampling removes modulo bias at the cost of a rule that is still easy to state exactly. Test vectors for seeds 0, 1 and 2^64-1 and rejection cases are in docs/spec/match.md section 4.

### C53 Tie rule: sole survivor wins; otherwise a tie among the last live bots

Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S04). After the last cycle, exactly one live bot wins; two or more survivors at the cycle limit tie (tied = survivors); no survivor (all remaining bots died in the last cycle) is a tie among the bots live at the start of that cycle. No tiebreak by process count or owned cells. Reason: it keeps the pMARS manual's 'single warrior remains' win and 'both lasted until time-out' tie, and treats bots that die in the same complete cycle as equal because each took the same number of steps. docs/spec/match.md section 8.

### C54 Default min separation: 100 empty cells between neighbouring bots

Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S04). MINSEPARATION is the minimum count of unowned cells between the end of one bot's block and the start of the next, going around the circular core; default 100, range 0..2^20. Placement is possible if and only if total bot length + bots * MINSEPARATION <= CORESIZE, else the error 'placement impossible: ...'. Reason: 100 is the default of the pMARS -d option and ICWS'94 draft MINDISTANCE (https://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/noble/man6/pmars.6.html), which pMARS measures between the first instructions of two warriors; pitfight deliberately counts empty cells between blocks instead, which makes impossibility an exact sum test independent of bot length and is stricter than 100 start-to-start. docs/spec/match.md sections 2 and 6.

### C55 Placement algorithm: shuffle, rotation, sequential gap draws; no retries

Implementer decision under C35 (S04). With the seeded generator: Fisher-Yates shuffle of bot ids (draws Draw(i+1) for i=K-1..1), rotation Draw(CORESIZE), then gaps g[k]=Draw(R+1) for k=0..K-2 from remaining slack R with the last gap taking the rest, start of each bot = previous start + length + MINSEPARATION + gap; 2K-1 draws, always made. Reason: it is deterministic and bounded, never needs a retry loop, and is exact for any input that passes the feasibility sum, so two implementations agree; the gap distribution is documented as non-uniform. Worked placements and impossible cases in docs/spec/match.md section 6.

### C56 Turn order: all live bots step once per cycle in ascending id; match ends at end of cycle

Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S04). A cycle is one step for each bot live at its start, in ascending bot id (ids = input order, not rotated); the match ends after the first cycle that leaves at most one live bot or that is cycle CYCLELIMIT; at least 2 and at most 2^20 bots; loaded cells carry the owner's bot id as writer; each bot starts with one process at its entry offset. Result fields: cycles, survivors, outcome (win or tie), winner, tied. Reason: it follows the pMARS definition of a cycle as one execution of each warrior and checking at the cycle end gives every bot the same number of steps; fixed id order is the simplest rule and fairness across orders is left to the tournament runner. docs/spec/match.md sections 5, 7 and 8.

### C57 isa package API: Opcode/Modifier/Mode uint8 types with Op*/Mod*/Mode* constants in spec order, Opcodes/Modifiers/Modes lists, String() mnemonics, Cell{Opcode,Modifier,AMode,AValue int32,BMode,BValue int32,Writer uint32}, EmptyCell

Plain typed constants and exported slices give later enumeration tests and the assembler one source for codes and mnemonics; int32 values and uint32 writer match isa.md section 1-2; no maps (C36).

### C58 vm core API: NewCore(size) (*Core, error) with ErrCoreSize, Size, Norm(int64) int32, Read(int64) Cell, Write(int64, Cell, bot uint32)

Addresses are int64 and Core.Norm is the single normalization (spec section 1), so sums cannot overflow and callers need no pre-reduction; Write sets the writer from the bot argument, Read never changes it; out-of-range size is an error rather than a panic.

### C59 vm operand API: Core.Resolve(pc, mode, value, bot) (Operand{Target, Snapshot, Post}, error) and Core.ApplyPostInc(PostInc, bot)

Splitting evaluation from post-increment lets S06 follow isa.md section 4 (evaluate A, evaluate B, execute, then post-increments on the field as it is in the core then); Resolve applies pre-decrements immediately as bot and returns ErrBadMode for a mode code above 7 instead of panicking.

### C60 VM execution and process queue API

S06 implementer decision under C35: Core.NewQueue(max, pcs...) returns (*Queue,error), normalizes initial addresses, validates MAXPROCESSES 1..2^20 and initial count, and copies input; Queue exposes Len, Dead and caller-owned Addresses. Core.Step(queue, bot, events) appends value events and executes one FIFO process, with dead queues a no-op. Queue uses a circular slice bounded by max for O(1) removal/requeue. Queues belong to their creating core and must not be copied; Step requires valid ISA codes and normalized cell fields and a nonzero bot id, matching the spec domain. Reason: arena can own one queue per bot, preserve deterministic FIFO order, and reuse its event buffer without shifting up to a million processes each turn.

### C61 VM integer event records and ordering

S06 implementer decision under C35: Event contains Kind (uint8 EventKind: CellWrite=0, ProcessSpawn=1, ProcessDeath=2), Bot uint32, PC int32, Address int32 and Cell isa.Cell. CellWrite holds the complete post-write cell including writer; process events have zero Cell. PC identifies the executed instruction, Address the written cell, child PC or dead PC. Only actual SPL child creation emits spawn; continuations and denied spawns emit nothing. All cell writes, including equal-value writes, appear in spec phase order; process events follow A/B post-increments. Reason: plain integer values retain intermediate writes for replay without I/O or clocks; caller-owned buffers avoid imposing event storage on the VM.

### C62 LICENSE present; README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md added; SPDX header on Go and shell files

Implementer decision under C35 and C32 (2026-10-17, owner-requested docs setup). LICENSE holds the AGPL-3.0 text per C32; NOTICE's last line points to it and AGENTS.md records its source and that it is never edited. README.md gives the overview, status, checks and license; CONTRIBUTING.md summarizes AGENTS.md rules and slicer use; PROJECT.md gets a background-only note at the top, body unchanged. Every Go file and scripts/env.sh start with SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later. Reason: the owner asked for the license and contributor docs; AGENTS.md stays the source of truth for agents.

### C65 asm API: Assemble(name, src) (Program{Cells, Entry}, error) with *asm.Error{File,Line,Col,Msg}

Implementer decision under C35 (S07). Assemble returns a Program holding the isa.Cell slice and the entry offset, and the first error as *asm.Error whose text is file:line:col: message (line and col start at 1, col counts bytes); on error the Program is the zero value. Reason: match.md section 5 needs an entry offset next to the cells, so a bare []isa.Cell would lose it; one error is enough for a bot file and keeps the first-error order well defined.

### C66 asm syntax: ';' comments, 'label:' definitions, case-insensitive opcodes/modifiers/ORG, case-sensitive labels, opcode[.mod] [A[, B]]

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, docs/spec/asm.md sections 1-4). One statement per line; any number of 'name:' labels before it; a label names the next instruction (or the program length if none follows); label names may not be an opcode or ORG; modes # $ * @ { < } > precede the operand expression, default $; an omitted operand is $0. Reason: the colon removes the Redcode ambiguity between a label and an opcode and is easy to lex by hand; the rest follows common Redcode practice.

### C67 asm default modifier: Redcode '94 table without MOD

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 4). DAT and NOP: F; MOV, SEQ, SNE: AB if A is #, else B if B is #, else I; ADD, SUB, MUL, DIV: AB, B, else F; SLT: AB if A is #, else B; JMP, JMZ, JMN, DJN, SPL: B. Reason: isa.md leaves the default to the assembler (section 2) and the Redcode '94 table lets the starter bots be written without explicit modifiers.

### C68 asm expressions: + - * / % and unary +/-, parentheses, labels relative to the instruction, int32 range

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 6). Precedence: unary, then * / %, then binary + -, left-associative; decimal literals only; / and % truncate toward zero like Go; division by zero and any result outside int32 (a literal may be 2147483648 so the minimum can be written) is an error; a label's value is index(label) - index(instruction holding the operand), and in ORG it is the absolute index; expression height is limited to 256. Reason: the smallest set that writes offsets and label differences, with one documented range that makes int64 arithmetic overflow-free.

### C69 asm output cells keep operand values as written (signed int32), not normalized to CORESIZE

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 6). The assembler does not know CORESIZE, and match.md section 5 stores Norm(v) when the bot is loaded, so Cell.AValue and BValue from Assemble may be negative. Reason: keeps a program independent of the core size and keeps listings and the round trip exact.

### C70 asm entry offset: the ORG expression directive, default 0, must lie in 0..L-1

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 5), answering the S04 note. 'ORG expression' on any line, at most once, with labels as absolute indexes; Program.Entry carries the value; without ORG it is 0. Reason: match.md section 5 needs an entry offset e in [0, L) and isa.md has none; ORG is the Redcode name for it.

### C71 asm errors: first error only, syntax errors before evaluation errors, fixed message texts and positions

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 7). Assembly stops at the first error; syntax errors are found in source order while reading, then undefined labels, evaluation errors, the empty program and the ORG range in the order asm.md lists; each message text and its position is a documented table that TestErrors checks. Reason: C17 asks for line and column errors, and fixed texts make them testable; one error per run avoids cascades.

### C72 pit asm <file>: prints a re-assemblable listing (ORG line, one canonical instruction per line); exit 1 on error, 2 on usage

Implementer decision under C35 (S07, asm.md section 9). On success stdout gets 'ORG e' then 'OPCODE.MODIFIER <mode><value>, <mode><value>' per cell with signed decimal values and explicit modifiers, nothing else; an assembly error or unreadable file prints file:line:col: message (or 'pit asm: <os error>') on stderr and exits 1 with empty stdout; a wrong argument count or an argument starting with '-' prints 'usage: pit asm <file>' and exits 2. The file name is printed exactly as given. The usage text now lists asm as implemented, marks the other commands 'not implemented yet' and adds exit code 1. Reason: a listing is both human-readable and valid source, which the S08 round trip needs; the exit codes extend C40.

### C75 pit run flags: --seed, --core-size, --cycle-limit, --max-processes, --min-separation, --json (S09)

Kebab-case flag per match.md config field, defaults from the spec; flags and bot files may be interleaved (pit run a.s b.s --seed 1) because that is the form the slice and the harness use.

### C76 pit run text output: config line, one line per bot, cycles, survivors, result (S09)

Plain line-oriented text with the fields of match.md section 8 plus each bot's file, length, start and entry_address (the absolute address Norm(start + entry offset) of its first process, not the offset e of match.md section 5), so a human and grep can read it; byte-identical for the same input (C16). Owner amendment 2026-10-18: the field was called 'entry'; it is entry_address (done in S11). With --replay S11 adds a last line 'replay: <hash>' (see the S11 record).

### C77 pit run --json: one JSON line with config, bots, cycles, survivors, outcome, winner, tied (S09)

A single line of fixed-order snake_case JSON with lists never null is the simplest machine-readable form for the later agent harness (C09). Owner amendment 2026-10-18 (done in S11): seed is a decimal string, not a JSON number, because JavaScript loses precision above 2^53; the bot field 'entry' is renamed entry_address (the absolute address, not the offset). With --replay a last field replay_hash is added.

### C78 pit run exit codes and error output (S09)

0 the match ran (win or tie); 1 a bot file, assembler, config or placement error, printed as 'pit run: <spec message>' on stderr with assembler errors bare as file:line:col like pit asm; 2 a usage error, so scripts can tell a bad invocation from a bad bot.

### C79 arena API: arena.Run(cfg, bots) returns Result, []vm.Event, error (S09)

Bot is cells plus entry offset so arena does not import the assembler; Result adds the Placement used; events cover steps only, not loading, leaving the replay slice free to choose its initial-state record; errors are *arena.Error with the three kinds of match.md section 1.

### C73 Disassembly is asm.Disassemble(Program) []byte; pit asm is its CLI entry point

Disassemble takes the Program (cells and entry) so the ORG line survives the round trip, and is the only listing formatter (moved from cmd/pit per C72); Writer is ignored. Reason: no binary cell format or cell source other than assembled source exists, so a separate pit disasm subcommand would print the same bytes as pit asm; documented in docs/spec/asm.md sections 8 and 9.

### C74 isa.md section 8 listings are asm blocks without the N: prefix

The three starter-bot listings in docs/spec/isa.md are tagged asm and the N: prefix moved into the trailing comment (; N: text), so TestRoundTripSpecExamples can extract and assemble them; the cells are unchanged.

### C83 Replay file: hand-written canonical JSON lines; the reader accepts only the writer's bytes (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35 (docs/spec/replay.md sections 1, 4, 8). The writer appends integers with strconv and fixed words by hand, so no map, no encoding/json and no string escaping touch the bytes (C36); the only strings are fixed words, the decimal seed and lowercase-hex hashes. The reader decodes each line with encoding/json for validation, then requires the line to equal what the writer would write for the parsed values, so Read then Write returns the same bytes and the file hash identifies the match. Line order: header, one load line per bot, cycle groups, end. Reason: byte stability across Go versions and one accepted spelling per replay; the cost is that hand-edited replays with other spacing are refused.

### C84 Replay v1 vocabulary: header, load, c/x/w/s/d body lines, end; a c line for every cycle and an x line for every step (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35 (replay.md section 4), amended by the owner's 2026-10-18 per-step execute record. Header: version, config (snake_case, seed a decimal string per the owner's C77 amendment), bots with id, hash, length, start, entry_address. load: the bot's Norm'd cells, so the file holds the initial core (C79 left the initial state to the replay). Body: c {n} for EVERY cycle 1..cycles (a cycle always has a step, since the match runs only while two bots are live); inside it one x {b,pc} line for EVERY step, silent ones (JMP, NOP, skipping tests) included, in ascending bot id; the step's events follow its x line and carry no bot or pc: w {a,c:[six ints]}, s {a}, d (no fields; its address is the step's pc), with at most one s or d and it last. A cell is [opcode,modifier,a_mode,a_value,b_mode,b_value] as isa codes, the writer being the step's bot. end: cycles (equal to the last c), survivors, outcome, winner, tied. All numbers stay below 2^31. The reader also checks that a bot steps only while its process count (1 + s - d) is above 0 and that survivors are the bots with a count above 0. Reason: compact (C07) and JS-safe (C19); a viewer rebuilds the core and shows the execution pointers of every cycle (S12, S15) without re-simulating; dropping b and pc from events removes redundancy. Size: the default-limit imp-vs-dwarf replay (5880 cycles) is 782675 bytes, about 133 bytes per cycle for two bots.

### C85 Replay v1 has no snapshot lines; seeking is the viewer's job (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35 (replay.md section 5). A viewer that wants to jump to a cycle keeps its own checkpoints while reading the file; a snapshot every K cycles would add up to CORESIZE cells per snapshot and would be a format change. Adding snapshot lines later is a new version number (replay.md section 7), with no optional fields in v1. Reason: smallest format that satisfies the slice; a later version can add them if a viewer needs it.

### C86 Replay hashes: SHA-256 hex of the file bytes; bot hash over entry offset plus raw assembled cells (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35 (replay.md section 6). Replay hash: SHA-256 of the whole file including the final line feed, lowercase hex. Bot hash: SHA-256 of the entry offset (4 bytes big endian) then 12 bytes per assembled cell (opcode, modifier, a_mode, a_value int32, b_mode, b_value int32, big endian; writer excluded), using the raw signed values of C69 so the hash does not depend on CORESIZE or placement. Readers treat the bot hash as opaque because the load lines are normalized. Reason: the slice asked for a stated encoding over the assembled cells; raw values keep a bot's identity independent of the match configuration.

### C87 Replay API: replay.Record, Read, Bytes, Hash, BotHash and Player (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35. Record(cfg, bots) runs the match and returns a Replay holding the config, bots as loaded, cycles (each with its []arena.Step) and the result; Bytes/Write give the file, Hash(data) and BotHash the hashes; Read(r) validates the whole file and returns a nil replay on any error, with *VersionError for an unknown version (message names the version); Player (NewPlayer, AdvanceTo, Core, Cycle, Steps, Live) rebuilds the core, the live process counts and the executed addresses of the current cycle by applying the file forward, which is what TestReplayEquivalence checks against the live core and live steps. Reason: one in-memory form shared by the pit run writer and later viewers, with no re-simulation.

### C88 arena.RunObserved: per-cycle hook with the live core; Run is built on it (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35, following the S09 note on C79 and amended for the per-step execute record. RunObserved(cfg, bots, observe) calls observe(0, core, nil) after loading and observe(c, core, steps) after each cycle with that cycle's []arena.Step in ascending bot id: Step{Bot, PC, Events}, PC being the address the step executed (the front of the bot's queue before it) and Events the step's VM events, empty for a silent step. The buffers are reused; observe must not modify the core or keep anything past the call. Run is RunObserved collecting the events, so its results and events are unchanged. To read the pc of a step the VM gets Queue.Front() (non-test vm source, one line). Reason: a flat event list cannot give cycle boundaries or the pc of steps that emit no event, and the equivalence test needs the live core and live steps at every cycle.

### C89 pit run --replay FILE writes the replay and prints its hash: 'replay: <hash>' or JSON replay_hash (S11)

S11 implementer decision under C35. The flag name --replay FILE follows the kebab-case flags of C75. With it, pit run records the match, writes FILE (a refused match writes nothing; a write error exits 1 with empty stdout) and adds the replay hash: a last text line 'replay: <64 hex>' and, with --json, a last field replay_hash; without the flag both are absent. Reason: C16 asks for the same result and replay hash on every run; printing the hash lets a script compare runs without shasum.

### C80 Starter golden table shape (S10)

Golden table pins the 6 unordered pairs of the four starter bots (lower id first, in the order imp, dwarf, replicator, scanner) at seeds 1, 2, 3 under the default config, 18 rows; the reverse order is the tournament's job (match.md section 7), and the table is small enough to review by hand.

### C81 Starter bot designs and parameters (S10)

Starter bots: dwarf bombs every 4th cell (3-cycle loop, separate bomb cell); replicator is 8 code cells plus an uncopied ptr cell, copies to +100, SPLs to the copy and loops back to copy 100 cells further; scanner examines every 3rd cell for 2600 passes per lap (7800 of 8000 cells, short of its own cells) and bombs with an empty cell. Parameters assume the default 8000-cell core; each is a plain source constant a later slice may tune.

### C82 Ship bots/ in release archives (S10)

Release archives include bots/ because README tells users to run pit run bots/imp.s bots/dwarf.s; build-release.sh copies the directory into each archive.

### C90 Starter scanner lap blind spot (S10)

The scanner's 2600-pass lap examines relative cells 10..7807, leaving 7808..7899 (inside placement's guaranteed-empty gap of 7900..7999) a ~92 cell blind spot for enemy code lying wholly there; accepted for the starter bot to keep it from examining its own cells; refines C81.

### C91 Tournament scoring: win 3, tie 1 each, loss 0; rank by points, wins, name (S13)

Implementer decision under C35 and C38 (S13). A won match scores 3 points, each bot of a tied match 1, a lost match 0; the scoreboard ranks by more points, then more wins, then the bot name in byte order, so no two bots share a rank. Reason: 3/1/0 is the usual Core War hill convention, keeps a tie worth less than half a win-and-loss pair so decisive bots rank above bots that only draw (the imp ties most matches), and the wins and name tiebreaks make the order total and independent of file order. docs/spec/tourney.md section 3.

### C92 Tournament pairings: every pair in both orders each round, one seed per round (S13)

Implementer decision under C35 (S13), answering the S04 note. Pairs are the unordered pairs of the name-sorted bots; each round plays every pair twice, as (a,b) then (b,a), so each bot is id 1 (first mover, match.md section 7) as often as id 2; all matches of a round use that round's seed. Reason: match ids are not rotated, so playing both orders is the simplest neutraliser and needs no change to the arena; a shared round seed keeps the two orders of a pair comparable. Matches are numbered along this fixed list, which is also the order results are scored and printed in (C36). docs/spec/tourney.md section 2.

### C93 Tournament seeds: Seed(round) = first SplitMix64 output seeded with the round number, rounds from 1 (S13)

Implementer decision under C35 and C36 (S13). Seed(r) is Next() of the match.md section 4 generator seeded with r, for r = 1..R; Seed(1)=10451216379200822465, Seed(2)=10905525725756348110. Reason: a pure function of the round with no clock and no math/rand, reusing the in-repo generator so it survives Go upgrades, and mixing spreads consecutive rounds over the whole 64-bit range instead of handing the placement small adjacent seeds. docs/spec/tourney.md section 2.

### C94 pit tourney flags and exit codes (S13)

Implementer decision under C35 (S13). pit tourney [flags] <dir>: --rounds N (default 100, the C18 acceptance count), --jobs N (default runtime.NumCPU; changes speed, never output), the four match config flags of pit run (--core-size, --cycle-limit, --max-processes, --min-separation; no --seed, rounds supply seeds), --json and --matches FILE; flags and the directory in any order. Bots are the *.s files directly in the directory, sorted by name and named without .s. Exit 0 ran, 1 directory, bot, config or file error, 2 usage (including rounds or jobs below 1). Reason: mirrors pit run (C75, C78) so one set of habits works for both, and the default 100 makes the C18 command short. docs/spec/tourney.md sections 1, 5 and 6.

### C95 pit tourney output: text scoreboard; --json scoreboard lines; --matches per-match JSON lines with decimal-string seeds (S13)

Implementer decision under C35 and C39 (S13). Default output is a config line, a scoring line and a right-aligned table (rank, bot, points, played, wins, ties, losses, mean_cycles); --json prints one object per bot (rank, bot, points, played, wins, ties, losses, cycles, mean_cycles); --matches FILE writes one object per match (index, round, seed, first, second, outcome, winner or null, cycles). Seeds are decimal strings (owner decision on C77). Both JSON forms are JSON lines with the same keys on every line. Reason: results stay as files with no database (C39) and uniform lines load straight into DuckDB read_json; the worker count is not printed so the bytes are the same for any --jobs. docs/spec/tourney.md section 5.

### C96 tourney package API: Pairings, Matches, Seed, Run(cfg, bots, rounds, jobs), Score, Format* (S13)

Implementer decision under C35 (S13). internal/tourney exports Pair/Pairings(n), Match/Matches(n, rounds), Seed(round), Bot{Name, Bot}, MatchResult{Match, Cycles, Winner (bot index, -1 for a tie)}, Run(arena.Config, []Bot, rounds, jobs) ([]MatchResult, error), Standing, Score(bots, results), and FormatText, FormatJSON and FormatMatches. Run uses a fixed-size goroutine pool fed match indexes over a channel; each worker writes only its own result slot, and an error is the one of the lowest failing match index. Reason: results are kept by match index, never by completion order or map iteration (C36), and the formatters live next to Score so a test can compare the exact scoreboard bytes across worker counts without the CLI.

### C97 Viewer frame model: cycle, owners, executed, live

S12 (C35). internal/tui Frame = {cycle, owners[addr] = last writer id (0 none), executed = [{bot, pc}] of that cycle in ascending bot order, live[bot-1] = process count: 1 at the start plus spawns minus deaths}; only the reported live value is clamped at 0, the running count after each event is not (the player keeps it below 0 when a replay has more deaths than processes). Plain JSON in testdata/viewer/frames.json so the web viewer (S15) can compare. Reason: an x record names only the stepping process, so executed addresses per cycle are all a viewer can know; the model is independent of the renderer (C19).

### C98 Viewer input: line-mode commands s, b, g, p, q

S12 (C35). pit view reads one command per line from stdin: s [N] step, b [N] back, g N seek (clamped to 0..last), p play/pause toggle, p N play N cycles, q quit, empty line steps (or pauses while playing); any line pauses a play. Bad input shows a message line and does not end the command. Reason: stdlib has no raw terminal mode and x/term is a dependency (C13); raw keys are a later change needing owner approval.

### C99 Viewer play: injectable clock, EOF rules, --delay

S12 (C35). tui.Player has no clock: the owner calls Tick once per frame while playing; pit view ticks every --delay ms (default 100) via an injectable after func. p plays to the last cycle and then pauses; play at the last cycle does nothing; p N plays N cycles. At end of input an open-ended play stops at once and a counted play (p N) finishes first, so piped scripts use p N and stay deterministic. Reason: testable play that always terminates.

### C100 Viewer layout: 72x20 grid, blocks of cells, reverse video

S12 (C35). The core is drawn as a grid of at most --cols x --rows characters (default 72x20, clamped to 1000), one character per cell when the core fits and otherwise per block of ceil(N/(cols*rows)) cells, rows labelled with the first address. A character shows the written owner with most cells in its block (lowest id on a tie) as a base-35 glyph (1-9, a-z, repeating) in one of 12 ANSI colours; '.' is unwritten; a block holding an executed address is reverse video. Bot lines (max 8) give live count and pc. Reason: 8000 cells need one 80x24 screen to watch a match; paging hides the action; flags let a bigger terminal show more.

### C101 pit view plumbing: runIn(args, stdin, stdout, stderr)

S12 (C35). cmd/pit gains runIn, run with a stdin reader; run(args, stdout, stderr) stays and passes an empty reader, so existing tests and the AGENTS.md signature hold. Reason: pit view is the first command that reads input and tests must feed it a strings.Reader.

### C102 Viewer fixture: imp vs dwarf, seed 24, core 24, 12 cycles

S12 (C35). testdata/viewer/fixture.jsonl = pit run bots/imp.s bots/dwarf.s --seed 24 --core-size 24 --min-separation 3 --cycle-limit 40 --replay FILE (a test regenerates it byte for byte). Core of 24 cells, imp at 3 (copies itself one cell ahead each cycle, so it reaches 14 and never wraps the core end), dwarf at 19 with its pointer cell at 22. The dwarf's bombs wrap the core end (22 + 4k mod 24), the one at cycle 11 lands on 14, the imp's newest copy, and at cycle 12 the imp executes that bomb and dies (live 0 against 1, bot 2 wins). Reason: small enough to derive every frame by hand, with writes by both bots, a bomb overwriting an imp copy, a wrapping write and a death.

### C103 S15 (C35): pit serve command shape

S15 (C35). 'pit serve [--port N] [--replays DIR] [--web DIR]' (net/http, stdlib) always binds 127.0.0.1 (default port 8080, 0 = free port), serves the viewer at / and the --replays directory at /replays/. Directories are opened as os.Root, so .. and symlinks cannot leave them (a refused path is 404). Only GET and HEAD are served (405 with Allow otherwise), and a request whose Host is not loopback or localhost gets 403 with no body (DNS-rebinding guard). Ctrl-C stops it. Reason: the smallest stdlib option that works around browsers blocking fetch from file://; loopback only means no flag can expose files to the network; S14 reuses newServeHandler.

### C104 S15 (C35): web viewer embedded into pit, not shipped beside it

S15 (C35). web/embed.go (package web, go:embed index.html style.css js) embeds the viewer files into the pit binary, excluding web/test; 'pit serve --web DIR' serves from disk instead for development. Reason: release archives hold one binary with no path to find web/ from, and embedding needs no change to scripts/build-release.sh.

### C105 S15 (C35): web viewer layout, colors, replay loading and test run

S15 (C35). Canvas: the core as square tiles in address order, tile colour per bot from last-writer id (golden-angle hues, hsl), empty cells dark grey, cells executed this cycle outlined in white (white tile if tiles are under 5 px); a core with more cells than pixels shows one tile per block of cells with the owner holding most cells, lowest id on a tie (as the terminal viewer). Side panel: per-bot live count and executed pc. Controls: first/back/play-pause/forward/last, speed (cycles per second), seek slider, keys Space/arrows/Home/End. Replay chosen with a file input, or '?replay=URL'. JS tests: 'node --test web/test/*.test.js' (node:test, shell glob). There is no package.json, so the Node must run .js files with ES module syntax by module-syntax detection: Node 26.12.0 is verified, older versions are not; CI runs the tests with the runner's Node and prints node --version. Reason: spec leaves layout open; the Go terminal viewer's block rule and frame model are the reference.

### C106 S15 (C35): JS replay parser strictness

S15 (C35). web/js/replay.js checks the line grammar and order, bot ids, address ranges, consecutive cycles, load cell counts and the end line against the cycles, and rejects other versions with 'replay: unsupported version N (this reader reads version 1)'. Config and bot-length ranges follow docs/spec/match.md section 1: core_size 1..1048576, max_processes 1..1048576, min_separation 0..1048576, cycle_limit 1..2^31-1, bot length 1..1048576, so a file cannot make the model allocate a huge core. It does not check exact writer bytes, placement consistency or that a bot steps only while live (the note from S11), so the model shows what is recorded. Live count = 1 + spawns - deaths, unclamped internally, shown as max(0, n) (as internal/tui). Reason: the viewer must not refuse files the Go reader accepts but should not trust ranges it indexes or allocates with.

### C107 Acceptance tests (internal/acceptance) build and run the real pit binary

TestMain builds ./cmd/pit with go build and the tests exec it from the repo root, because package main cannot be imported and the criteria name the command; goldens are internal/acceptance/testdata/imp_dwarf_seed1.result.txt and .hash.txt, and the golden hash is also compared with fullHash in internal/replay/replay_test.go.

### C108 Second shared viewer fixture with SPL: testdata/viewer/spl_fixture.jsonl and spl_frames.json

frames.json had no spawn or death, so live-process parity of the Go and web viewers was unchecked; the pair is written by pit run from testdata/viewer/spl_splitter.s and spl_sitter.s (seed 1, core 24), its frames derived by hand, and read by internal/tui TestFrames and web/test/model.test.js.

### C109 Flag interleaving and -- in pit run, tourney and view

cmd/pit parseInterleaved splits args with the flag package's own rules before one Parse: a non-bool flag without =value takes the next argument as its value even if that is --, and only a -- in a flag position ends the flags. One helper replaces three copies (run, tourney, view). Reason: the old test for a consumed -- could not tell a terminator from a flag value, so --replay -- turned later flags into files.

### C110 Replays are written through a temp file and rename

pit run --replay writes to .NAME.tmpPID.N in the same directory, syncs it and renames it over FILE, removing the temp on any failure, so FILE is never partial. A replaced regular file keeps its mode (the temp file is chmodded to it before the rename); a new file gets 0644 less the umask. A target that exists and is not a regular file (symlink, device, pipe) is written in place, because a rename would replace it. Reason: atomic result for files, no surprise for /dev/null or links, and no mode change on overwrite.

### C111 Tournament events-off path is a nil observer, not new API

tourney.play calls arena.RunObserved(cfg, bots, nil), which already keeps only one cycle of events; arena.Run is the one that keeps all events. TestRunKeepsNoEvents measures tourney.Run allocating about 1.38 MB for 6 matches (two imps that tie at 80000 cycles and a bot that dies at once, one round) against 11.5 MB for the events of the same matches kept by arena.Run. No new arena function; unexported tourney.playMatch is the test seam for the concurrency test. Reason: smallest change that removes the memory growth.

### C112 Arena limits exported and shared with replay

arena exports MaxCoreSize (= vm.MaxCoreSize), MaxCycleLimit, MaxMaxProcesses, MaxMinSeparation, MaxBots, MaxBotLength; internal/replay reads them instead of keeping copies. Reason: one source for the match.md section 1 limits.

### C113 pit view skips command lines over 64 KiB with a message

pit view reads input with a bufio.Reader instead of bufio.Scanner; a line of more than 65536 bytes (without the line break) is read to its end, ignored, shows 'line too long' on screen, and the session goes on (exit 0). Reason: bounded memory, and a pasted long line no longer ends the session with 'token too long'.

### C114 pit serve accepts Host localhost. with the root dot

isLocalHost trims one trailing dot before comparing with localhost (RFC 1034 root form of the same name). Other names with a dot, and 127.0.0.1., stay refused. Reason: same name, no rebinding risk added.

### C115 Acceptance package keeps no doc.go; package comment moves to acceptance_test.go

S23 (C35). internal/acceptance/doc.go is deleted and its package comment now heads acceptance_test.go, so the directory holds only _test.go files, as README.md and AGENTS.md say (test-only). go build ./..., go vet ./... and go test ./... are unchanged. Reason: the file existed only to carry the package comment, and a non-test file contradicted 'test-only'.

### C116 asm.md bomber listing is an asm block under TestRoundTripSpecExamples

S23 (C35). The listing printed by pit asm for the bomber in docs/spec/asm.md section 9 is tagged asm, not text, because a listing is itself valid source (asm.md section 9). TestRoundTripSpecExamples now round-trips it and counts 5 asm blocks in asm.md; TestSpecListing checks that the asm block after the bomber equals the output of pit asm. Reason: one place checks every runnable listing in the specs; the text tag left it covered by a string comparison only.

### C33 CI deferred

Owner decision 2026-10-15. CI is deferred; no CI host is chosen. Checks run locally (see the in-repo Go cache and checks constraint).

*Retired: Owner lifted the CI deferral 2026-10-17; GitHub Actions chosen. Successor: C63.*

### C42 LICENSE left absent; pending state recorded in AGENTS.md and NOTICE; SPDX header on Go and shell files

Implementer decision under C35 and C32 (S02). LICENSE is not created because the owner has not supplied the AGPL-3.0 text; AGENTS.md has a License section stating it is PENDING and that the text must not be written, fetched or edited, and NOTICE's last line points to it. Every Go file and scripts/env.sh start with SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later. Reason: slice step 5 allows either outcome; the flag in both files keeps a missing LICENSE from reading as an oversight.

*Retired: LICENSE now exists (C32 override 2026-10-17); superseded by C62. Successor: C62.*

## Assumptions

### C20 Name: keep placeholder bot-arena

PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION - not decided. Placeholder name is "bot-arena" (CLI examples use "arena"). PROJECT.md gives no recommendation and no alternatives. (PROJECT.md Open decisions 1)

*Retired: Settled by owner decision C26 (2026-10-15)..*

### C21 ISA: original ISA strongly inspired by Redcode semantics

PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION - not decided. Recommendation: an original ISA strongly inspired by Redcode semantics, small enough to specify in a few pages; Redcode compatibility can come later as a mode. Alternatives: (a) implement a subset of the Redcode ICWS'94 standard (body of existing warriors and literature); (b) design a new small ISA (freedom, distinct identity). (PROJECT.md Open decisions 2)

*Retired: Settled by owner decision C27 (2026-10-15)..*

### C22 Core language: Rust core + WASM, TypeScript viewer

PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION - not decided. Recommendation: Rust for assembler, VM and tournament runner, compiled to WASM so the web viewer can run live matches with the identical core; web viewer in plain TypeScript + canvas, no framework. Alternatives: (A) all TypeScript (Node CLI, browser viewer; one language, simpler toolchain, slower tournaments); (B) Python stdlib core plus a JS viewer (fastest to prototype; too slow for large tournaments without optimization). Rust + wasm-pack (or equivalent) needs owner approval per dependency rules. (PROJECT.md Stack recommendation, Open decisions 3)

*Retired: Settled by owner decision C28 (2026-10-15)..*

### C23 Replay format: versioned JSON lines for v1

PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION - not decided. Recommendation: versioned JSON lines for v1 (simple, debuggable), binary format later if size matters. Alternative named in the data model: a periodic snapshot plus a delta log. (PROJECT.md Open decisions 4, Core concepts: Replay)

*Retired: Settled by owner decision C29 (2026-10-15)..*

### C24 Default match parameters: Redcode '94 hill norms

PENDING OWNER CONFIRMATION - not decided. Recommendation: start from Redcode '94 hill norms (core 8000, cycles 80000, max processes 8000) and tune.
